title: Feature execution state (feature.json)
description: FEAT-14 D-01: ten top-level keys, additionalProperties false at every closed level. There is no `phase` property — `phase` and `status` collapsed into `status` alone under D-09/D-10. There is no `status` property either, as of FEAT-41 T-07: the feature's station is recorded in plan.yaml's own top-level `status`, and ONE file records it. Because additionalProperties is false, a feature.json that still carries `status` is now a schema error rather than a tolerated duplicate — which is what makes the single record enforceable instead of merely documented. FEAT-59 adds four OPTIONAL top-level keys (`mission`, `judgements`, `rework`, `budget_decisions`) and three optional runs-entry keys (`started_at`, `ended_at`, `tokens`): the judgement and spend ledger the operator audits after the fact (SC-15, SC-18, SC-21). Every one is optional because every feature.json on disk predates them; each is written only by feature-record.py.

feature_id.description: The feature's own identifier, e.g. FEAT-14-feature-json-schema. No demonstrated code reader at the FEAT-14 census; kept because the eleven-key boundary starts at SPEC 11.3's ten and the burden of proof is on removing a key, never on keeping one already there.

branch.description: The feature's branch name, or the literal string 'none' when unset — check-state.sh INV-6 already treats 'none' as unset via PLACEHOLDER_UNSET, so this stays a plain string rather than nullable. No demonstrated code reader.

pr.description: The feature's pull request number, or null before one exists. READ BY CODE as of FEAT-26: check-state.sh's INV-28 warns when a Done feature leaves it null, gh-sync.py's record-pr derives and writes it, and ship threads it before the terminal status write. JSON's native null replaces the YAML-era placeholder string 'none' (T-04 rewrites those to null).

review_sha.description: Read by check-state.sh's val("review_sha") check against PLACEHOLDER_UNSET. The literal string 'none' is a legal, unset value for the same reason as branch.

cycles_used.description: Read by check-state.sh's val("cycles_used") check against the FAIL-run count.

max_total_cycles.description: No demonstrated code reader at the FEAT-14 census; kept because the eleven-key boundary starts at SPEC 11.3's ten and the burden of proof is on removing a key, never on keeping one already there.

runs.description: Read by check-state.sh's per-run loop, entry.get("id"/"squad"/"verdict").

squad.description: The squad that executed the run.

agent.description: Names the agent that executed the run. ABSENCE MEANS THE ENTRY PREDATES FEAT-31 and is not an error: this key is deliberately NOT in `required`, because a schema-level requirement would deny every entry already on disk, and check-domain.sh's post sweep reaches feature.json files a change never touched. The requirement is POSITIONAL instead and lives in feature_schema.py (D-23).

code_grade.description: BUG-1080. Present ONLY as `n_a`, declaring that this validator run graded a specification and no code, which is the plan-phase panel DEC-207 legalises. INV-6 then requires no pinned review_sha for it, because there is no commit to pin. ABSENCE MEANS THE RUN REVIEWED CODE and a pin IS required — the opposite default from `agent` above, and deliberately so: every entry already on disk predates this key and did review code, so a benign absence would retire INV-6 across the whole corpus. The enum is closed for the same reason; an unrecognised value must fail rather than exempt.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which feature-record.py run-start appended this entry; read by feature-record.py spend, which sums ended_at minus started_at into the feature's wall-clock minutes (SC-18). ABSENCE MEANS THE ENTRY PREDATES FEAT-59 and is not an error; such an entry contributes zero minutes.

ended_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant at which feature-record.py run-end closed this entry; read by feature-record.py spend. ABSENCE MEANS THE RUN IS STILL OPEN, or predates FEAT-59 — both contribute zero minutes, never an estimate.

tokens.description: Tokens this run consumed, MEASURED by the caller from the OMP transcript on disk and passed to feature-record.py run-end, or null when no measurement was taken. Read by feature-record.py spend, which sums the integers and prints null when no run carries one (SC-18). Null is never 0 and is never estimated: a reader must be able to tell an unmeasured run from a free one. ABSENCE MEANS THE ENTRY PREDATES FEAT-59.

max_total_runs.description: Read by check-state.sh's _as_budget(val("max_total_runs")). Optional: SPEC 11.3 says it may be omitted to inherit harness.json's default.

mission.description: The harness's own proportionality judgement for this feature, written by feature-record.py set-mission after grilling and read by check-state.sh, which refuses a mission change with no matching `judgements[]` entry (SC-01, SC-21). `patch` runs build → qa → review → ship with no plan.yaml and no panel; `plan` runs the collapsed plan phase first. ABSENCE MEANS THE FEATURE PREDATES FEAT-59, or has not been graded yet; /harness-plan refuses to start on it.

judgements.description: The append-only ledger of every autonomous judgement the harness made on this feature, written by feature-record.py judgement and read by check-state.sh (which refuses a mission change, re-gate or succession with no matching entry) and by the operator, who audits it after the fact instead of ruling in-flight (SC-21). ABSENCE MEANS NO JUDGEMENT HAS BEEN RECORDED, which for a feature run under FEAT-59 is itself what check-state.sh flags.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the judgement was recorded.

by.description: The persona that judged, e.g. harness-orchestrator or harness-validator-lead.

kind.description: Which class of judgement this is: the five SC-21 names, closed so an unrecognised class fails rather than slips past the operator's audit.

decision.description: What was decided, in the vocabulary of its kind: patch|plan, substance|form|proportionality, the task ids re-gated, continue|downgrade|stop.

reason.description: The one-line reason; capped so the ledger stays a ledger (DEC-150) and a reason that needs a paragraph goes in the run's digest instead.

rework.description: The operator's one rework ruling, recorded at signature by feature-record.py set-rework (SC-15): the orchestrator loops inside these bounds without asking. `wall_clock_minutes` is read by the OMP hook's SPEND advisory after build entry (SC-19). ABSENCE MEANS NO RULING WAS RECORDED — a feature signed before FEAT-59, or a patch mission that never reached one.

rounds.description: Rework rounds the orchestrator may run before returning awaiting_user.

wall_clock_minutes.description: Wall-clock budget for the validate/fix loop; exceeding it ADVISES and never refuses (DEC-198).

decision.description: Where the ruling is recorded, e.g. a plan.yaml approval.rulings reference or a DEC id.

budget_decisions.description: One entry per raise of `max_total_cycles`, appended by feature-record.py raise-cycles alongside the raise itself, and read by check-state.sh, which refuses a `max_total_cycles` above the template default with no matching entry (SC-15, DEC-157). ABSENCE MEANS THE BUDGET WAS NEVER RAISED, or was raised before FEAT-59.

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant of the raise.

decision.description: The recorded user decision the raise rests on, e.g. a DEC id or plan.yaml ruling reference.

github.description: Read by gh-sync.py's load_recorded and by check-state.sh INV-21. Present only once a feature is mirrored to GitHub; no property inside is required.

milestone.description: The GitHub milestone number, or null.

parent.description: The parent issue number, or null.

issues.description: Task id to mirrored GitHub issue number.

source_issues.description: The GitHub issue numbers this feature was planned from, mirrored from plan.yaml's top-level source_issues by gh-sync.py open. Read by gh-sync.py's `closes` renderer. Absent or empty is legal: a feature planned before this key existed carries none, and a feature can be planned from no ticket at all.

typed.description: Provenance of native GitHub Issue Type application, keyed by "parent" or a task id (D-20). "created" means Harness created the issue and has not yet applied its type; the promoted boolean true means Harness created it and applied the type; "adopted" means the number was adopted through --parent and Harness never created or types it. ABSENCE of an entry means provenance is UNKNOWN and is never typed - not on this run, not on any later one.

build_entry.description: The mirror Build DAG's own status, written by gh-sync.py. Five states, and absence is meaningful: "opened" - open completed with github.sync enabled and github.repo pinned; the milestone, the parent and every task sub-issue are recorded. "recovery-required" - sync was enabled and the repo pinned, but the run stopped on a temporary environmental no-go BEFORE any remote-mutating call; Build may proceed, but MERGE is refused until a re-run records opened. "not-applicable" - github.sync is false or absent, an approved no-mirror delivery mode that gates nothing; NOT reached when sync is enabled and github.repo is unpinned, which is a local configuration error that records nothing and blocks Build (D-09). "recovered-terminal" - written only by gh-sync.py recover-terminal for an already-merged feature whose mirror was never opened; milestone plus the parent and source issues only, never task sub-issues. ABSENT (the key is missing) - no Build entry ever completed: open never ran, or github.sync was enabled with github.repo unpinned, or the run failed after creating at least one remote object, or it exited on a caller or contract error; Build refuses.

factory.description: Read by factory_decompose.py's load_factory, factory_claim.py's issue_number, and check-state.sh INV-24. Present only once a feature is decomposed by the factory; no property inside is required.

repo.description: The factory repo name, or null.

parent.description: The parent issue number, or null.

issues.description: Task id to mirrored GitHub issue number.

typed.description: Provenance of native GitHub Issue Type application, keyed by "parent" or a task id (D-20). "created" means Harness created the issue and has not yet applied its type; the promoted boolean true means Harness created it and applied the type; "adopted" means the number was adopted through --parent and Harness never created or types it. ABSENCE of an entry means provenance is UNKNOWN and is never typed - not on this run, not on any later one.
